To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the flow in the vicinity of a cerebral anurysm becomes chaotic; (ii) chaotic transport is quantifiable; (iii) fractal patterns can be measured and (iv) the fractal dimension is the most suitable parameter to characterise the chaotic transport in the flow.
the fractal dimension is a useful parameter to characterize the chaotic flow in the vicinity of an aneurysm and that it might be used as an indicator of its condition.

chaotic advection in a 3D cerebral artery segment can be quantitatively characterized by the information dimension and that the chaotic properties of the flow are strongly dependent on the aneurysmal sac size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the flow dynamics in a real three dimensional cerebral aneurysmal sac.
the development and application of a new method for the analysis of fractal structures that are emerging in a three dimensional flow field.
the study of the effect of aneurysmal malformations on the transport of blood and the possible implications on the condition of this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chaotic advection in cerebral aneurysms is a relevant factor for the development and growth of this pathologic condition.
chaotic advection in a 3D cerebral artery segment can be characterised by the information dimension and the Lyapunov exponent.
the fractal dimension is a useful tool to describe chaotic mixing and to characterise blood transport close to an aneurysm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by investigating the chaotic properties of the flow in the vicinity of cerebral aneurysms, it is possible to gain a better understanding of the flow-related formation of aneurysms.
the information dimension is an important parameter for the characterisation of chaotic advection, and that it can be measured in a robust way even in complex 3D geometries.
the chaotic behaviour of a blood flow in the vicinity of a cerebral anaurysm might be a relevant parameter for the formation and growth of aneurysms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fractal properties of the flow can be used to characterise the flow in complex geometries, such as those found in the human brain.
the information dimension is a useful tool to characterise the chaotic advection of the blood flow in the proximity of the aneurysl sac.
the information dimension is the most reliable parameter that could be used to characterise chaotic mixing in the vicinity of cerebral aneurysms.
